text: Weekend brunch chaos - forty minutes standing with two hungry kids, no table in sight, and the waffle that finally came was burnt.
Queued 25 minutes for a table, then they brought a latte instead of my flat white and acted like I was the problem.
Fantastic, forty minutes for a takeaway cappuccino on a Sunday. They really outdid themselves this weekend.
Sunday rush mein group ke liye zero seats, and one cheese toast plus chai cost us 400. Bheed aur price dono galat.
Weekend surge order: paneer sandwich missing, two wrong drinks, arrived 75 minutes late. Brunch ruined at home.
The place was packed and staff snapped at my son for asking where his shake was. Thirty-five minutes for a kids drink.
Everyone online says cute Sunday spot. Reality: stood holding a waffle in a queue of twenty, nowhere to sit, 260 gone.
Sunday delivery arrived so late the pasta had gone cold and clumped into one sad brick. Sauce leaked into the bag too.
Ordered my usual in on a busy Sunday - cappuccino was burnt and watery, and support just blamed the rush. Slipping badly.
Team brunch order of eleven: arrived an hour late, three chais missing, bags unlabelled. Weekend shift clearly cannot cope.
Forget working here on a Sunday - wall-to-wall crowd, queue blocking every table, and the wifi buckled under it all.
Queue was endless, counter v slow. One espresso = 20 min wait. Never again on sunday morning.
Cheesecake arrived squashed flat against the box lid, glaze smeared everywhere. A 290-rupee mess on a Sunday afternoon.
Strawberry shake tipped over inside the bag and soaked everything; they also sent one instead of two. Weekend disaster.
Sunday order hostel mein 80 min late aaya, fries ekdum thande aur soggy. Brunch ka mood kharab.
Long weekend queue with cranky kids, 30 minutes for fries. They were crisp and tasty when they landed, I will admit.
Waffle was genuinely great, but every table taken so we ate it standing on the pavement outside. Sunday fail.
Filter coffee itself was excellent, but the brunch crowd made it feel like a railway platform. Could not enjoy the dabarah ritual.
Avocado toast took over an hour on Sunday and reached cold, sourdough gone limp. Expected much better for 380.
Pure bheed thi yaar, plug bhi nahi mila, group poora adjust nahi hua. Chai achi thi bas, warna waste trip.
Fifteen-minute line for a croissant that turned out dry and day-old. Sunday crew looked completely overwhelmed.
My usual Sunday latte took 25 minutes and the table we finally got was still sticky from the last party. Not the norm here.
Brunch order for eight: no labels, two iced lattes swapped for cold brews, one cup unsealed. Guesswork at the office.
Fries arrived cold and the blueberry muffin was squashed under the drink cups. Sunday delivery needs work.
Family lunch order took 90 minutes in the weekend rush; pasta lukewarm, garlic smell long gone. Kids ate bread instead.
Thirty-minute queue, then a server hovered till we gave up the table. Matcha was decent but the vibe was pure rush.
Shake ka lid tight nahi tha, bag mein half spill ho gaya. Sunday counter itna busy tha ki check kisine kiya hi nahi.
Pretty pink spot for photos, but staff were too slammed to even smile. Rose latte looked better than it tasted.
Weekend dinner landed 75 minutes late - pasta cold, fries limp. The one warm thing was the hot chocolate, thankfully.
They handed me a latte instead of my usual flat white and the queue was too long to bother going back. Sunday tax.
Every two-seater had a laptop or a brunch crowd hovering for it. Gave up after one cold brew and worked from the bus stop.
The waffle was genuinely divine - crisp, maple-drenched. The 35-minute brunch queue to get it, less divine.
Kids loved the fries and shake, but six tables for all of Indiranagar on a Sunday is rough - we ate half standing.
Counter moved quicker than expected in the rush, but the croissant was dry at the edges. Mixed bag this Sunday.
Bheed bohot thi, seat milne mein 20 min. Par chai aur cheese toast worth it the - 400 mein three log sorted.
Sandwich arrived lukewarm after the weekend surge, but the paneer tikka filling was genuinely flavourful. Mixed feelings.
Sunday rush clearly slows them down - flat white took a while but the pour was still textbook. Forgiving because usuals are good.
Adorable pink cafe, mad Sunday line, decent cheesecake. Worth one visit but maybe not a second queue.
Weekend dinner order ran 50 minutes over the estimate, but everything arrived and the pasta was properly spicy.
Sunday is not for laptops here - noise everywhere. Still, the cold brew was smooth and nobody actually asked me to leave.
Office brunch drop: ek chai spill ho gaya, baaki sab labels ke saath sahi tha. Weekend packing thodi careful ho sakti hai.
Rose latte was too sweet for me this time, though the rose petal aroma is lovely. Ambience pretty but packed wall to wall.
Sunday delivery 50 min lagi, but fries 160 mein kaafi the aur crispy bhi. Slow but cheap, so theek hai.
Queue looked scary but moved okay; cappuccino was hot and proper. Just plan extra time on weekends here.
Rider was quick but the waffle box got squashed under the shakes - edges soggy, centre still crisp. Half a win.
Staff were kind and found us two stools, but a party of four in a six-table cafe on Sunday is a squeeze. Shake won the kids.
Grabbed a kulhad chai to go - waited in the tourist line for 15 minutes, but that first gingery sip made up for it.
Ordered in to skip the Sunday crowd - blueberry muffin arrived fresh, though the bag was crushed on one side.
Iced latte was perfectly chilled; the cheese toast beside it turned soggy in the same bag. Bit of a split verdict.
Sunday treat: cappuccino plus croissant now crosses 400. Quality still there, but my weekend ritual is getting pricey.
Weekend pe kaam nahi hua, crowd zyada tha aur plug occupied. Cold brew solid thi, toh visit bura nahi gaya.
Waited 20 minutes for a table while the kids circled the pastry fridge; the waffle that followed earned forgiveness.
Sunday dinner at home - order was late but the arrabbiata was fiery and fresh once it finally reached.
Weekend office order: good labelling but one filter coffee arrived as a chai. Ten happy people, one confused.
Cheesecake travelled mostly well - glaze slightly smudged on one corner. Taste itself was still wonderful at home.
Busy Sunday brunch but absolutely worth it - waffle crisp, berries fresh, pink room buzzing. Come before 10.
Packed house yet the kids got their shakes and fries without fuss. Short wait, happy plates, good Sunday.
Despite the weekend crowd spilling onto the pavement, my espresso was in hand in six minutes. Respect.
Cheap chai, buzzing Sunday vibe, managed a shared table. Bheed hai but yahi toh scene hai.
Ordered filter coffee to the guesthouse on a lazy Sunday - came sealed, still hot, decoction strong. Lovely.
Dev sent a little extra mint chutney with my sandwich because he knows I like it. Busy room, warm hearts.
Sunday lunch landed right on the estimate - pasta hot, sauce fiery, portion decent for two of us.
Weekend delivery done right - fries still had crunch, hot chocolate fully sealed. Kids approve, parents relieved.
Grabbed the last window pair, shared a Basque cheesecake, watched the Sunday crowd ebb and flow. Charming chaos.
Came at 8:30 to beat the brunch wave - quiet hour with cold brew and a plug, then the lovely chaos rolled in.
Ordered to the hostel for the whole gang - cheese toast and fries under 500 for three of us. Arrived warm. Solid.
Queue was out the door but they were calling tickets fast; flat white was silky as ever. Weekend crew is on it.
Waffle box arrived a bit late on Sunday but perfectly packed - maple separate, berries fresh, still warm.
Big Sunday pickup: twelve croissants and eight chais, all bagged and labelled. Pickup counter could use one more hand.
Stood in the famous Sunday line and honestly? Worth every minute for that dabarah-frothed filter coffee.
They pushed two little tables together for our family of five without being asked. Pasta was hearty, kids happy.
Cheesecake slice arrived upright and gorgeous - the pink-stamped kraft bag is such a nice touch for delivery.
Sunday crowd tha but vibes mast - fries, chai aur dost, under 350 per head. Bas thoda wait.
Usual cappuccino grabbed fast even on Sunday, though I notice it is 10 rupees up since last month. Still loyal.
Kids' waffle order reached home intact and warm - maple on the side, no soggy edges. Loud Sunday at home instead.
Rose latte is as pretty as the room - floral, silky. Packed to the rafters but that is Sunday at brew.
Snagged the corner seat at opening, got real work done over an iced latte before the brunch crowd took over.
Fifteen-item team brunch delivered - everything correct and labelled, just fifteen minutes behind schedule. Dependable.
Even in the weekend rush the sandwich arrived warm and toasted. Delivery beat the estimate by ten minutes.
Ordered a matcha to the hotel room after a long morning - whisked properly, no clumps, arrived quickly. Impressed.
Grabbed fries between plans - counter was slammed but they moved fast, and 160 for that crunch is fair.
Sunday dinner for four - pasta, shakes, fries all present and warm, nothing missing. Weekend win for delivery.
Perched on a counter stool for a fast cappuccino amid the brunch storm. Efficient little operation, this.
Lazy Sunday delivered: cheesecake and a cinnamon roll, both neat in the box, icing intact. Indulgent done right.
Even with a queue behind me the filter coffee was frothed properly, no shortcuts. Consistent even under pressure.
Hot chocolate reached us properly hot with the marshmallows riding in a separate little pot. Thoughtful packing.
Sunday bheed mein bhi delivery ka chai garam aur strong tha. Seat nahi mili shop pe toh hostel pe enjoy kiya.
The perfect Sunday brunch: shared waffle, two flat whites, sun through the pink window, and a table we never wanted to leave.
Staff found us space, kids got their shakes fast, and the split-flap board kept everyone entertained. Sunday sorted.
Weekend queue looked terrifying and moved like a machine - espresso in four minutes. Fastest counter in Indiranagar.
Best cheap Sunday scene - chai, fries, three friends, one shared table, total under 500. Student heaven boss.
Found the cutest pink cafe in Indiranagar on my last morning - filter coffee, bustling brunch crowd, pure joy.
Meera had my cappuccino going the second I walked in on a packed Sunday. That is what being a regular feels like.
Brunch in bed: waffle arrived crisp, maple syrup in its own pot, berries unfazed. Delivery perfection on a Sunday.
Family pasta night delivered hot in 30 minutes - no soggy anything, kids cleared their bowls. Best Sunday in ages.
That strawberry cheesecake is worth every minute of the Sunday queue - caramelised edges, fresh glaze, happy dance.
Rare empty Sunday-morning seat, cold brew, two hours of quiet before the brunch wave. Grateful this place exists.
Brunch pickup for the whole team - a dozen bakes, all fresh, every bag labelled by name. Not one crumb out of place.
Cheap aur tasty delivery - cheese toast garam, bubbly cheddar intact. Sunday study lunch sorted under 300.
My daughter's first cafe hot chocolate and they made it special - extra marshmallows, patient smiles, pink everywhere.
Showed up at 9 sharp on a Sunday - zero wait, flawless flat white, back on the road by 9:15. Weekend miracle.
Rose latte in a sunlit pink corner while the brunch crowd hummed - this place is a whole mood board.
Saturday pit stop done perfectly - cappuccino and a warm croissant, ten minutes total, out the door smiling.
Waffle and a thick shake delivered for a lazy morning - everything sealed, nothing tipped, tasted fresh off the griddle.
Full family feast ordered in - pasta, fries, two shakes, all correct and fast. Sunday cooking avoided, zero regrets.
Sunday ritual intact: my filter coffee, the regulars' nod from Kabir, the split-flap board flipping over. Home.
Skipped the crowd, got a matcha delivered - still properly whisked, ceremonial and calming. Sunday rescued at home.
Study group turned into lunch - split a paneer sandwich and chais, staff let us linger. Paisa vasool Sunday.
One kulhad chai for the road on a busy Sunday - gingery, hot, five-minute wait. Bengaluru keeps surprising me.
Office brunch delivery for nine - timed perfectly to our break, every drink labelled, zero mistakes. Seamless.
The kids call it the pink waffle house now. Two waffles demolished, staff waved goodbye by name. Sunday favourite.
Cinnamon roll warm from the oven, cream cheese icing still soft, buzzing room around us. Bliss.
Weekend morning, empty tables till ten, espresso and quiet - this cafe knows how to host a solo morning too.
Ordered a cheap feast to the hostel - fries crisp, chai still hot, everything under 350. Sundays unlocked.
Zoya spotted me in the Sunday queue and had my latte ticket ready. In and out in five. This is service.
Anniversary dessert delivered - cheesecake pristine, glaze glossy, kraft bag cute. They made our quiet Sunday special.
Quick pickup on the way to the park - rose milk for the kids, packed careful, ready in minutes. Lovely crew.
Best waffle in town, now even at my door - crisp edges survived the ride, maple on point. Sunday champion.
Jet-lagged and hungry, ordered a paneer tikka sandwich to the hotel - arrived fast, toasted, delicious. First win in Bengaluru.
Sunday scene sorted - cheese toast, chai, noisy happy room, bill under 300. Yeh jagah alag hai boss.
